blocks.text: Once the pact is sealed, Dina Beg prepared his contingent and moved his own camp toward the coming theater of war. Messages go out to the Sikh chiefs, gifts and pay are arranged, and the allied force begins to gather in strength for the push toward Jalandhar.

As the Khalsa assembles, the opposing Pathans drew up opposite and their presence unsettles the Nawab's men. Dina Beg's camp senses the seriousness of the clash, and the Nawab leans on Wadbhag Singh to steady nerves and bring the Sikh force fully into the field.

Wadbhag Singh reassures him that the Guru's Panth does not withdraw once it has given its word. The page closes with the alliance hardened, the message to the Singhs fulfilled, and both sides poised for the opening engagement toward Jalandhar.
